divergences.old: confluence attachment download fetching the attachment's _links.download, with the token, from whatever host an absolute link names
divergences.toil: The token goes only to baseUrl's origin: an absolute download link on another host has its path and query re-pointed at baseUrl, with a CONFLUENCE_ATTACHMENT_HOST warning. Relative links, the usual shape, still resolve under baseUrl (#78 item 1)
divergences.why: A server-supplied URL must not carry the user's credential to a host they didn't configure. A change a principle requires, so the integration makes it before a live run (CLAUDE.md, The command contract).

divergences.old: Ids, space keys and labels put into URL paths as given, so a value with .., /, \, ? or # changes which resource a request names (page delete ../space/DOCS sends DELETE /rest/api/space/DOCS)
divergences.toil: Each id, space key and label is encoded as one path segment, so /, \, ?, #, ; and % in it are part of the name (label a/b is sent as a%2Fb). One that is a . or .. segment, bare or between encoded slashes (../space/DOCS), is refused with INVALID_INPUT before any request by core's requests.path bound (docs/bounds.md). Plain values are sent unchanged (#78 item 4)
divergences.why: The write gate approves the command a caller asked for; a value must not turn a page delete into a space delete. An agent can be handed such a value by text in the content it reads.

divergences.old: confluence page delete and attachment delete as commands of every front door
divergences.toil: CLI only, still behind the write gate: they are not MCP tools
divergences.why: Deletes are never exposed through MCP (CLAUDE.md, Writes).

divergences.old: confluence attachment download writing to a file that already exists
divergences.toil: Refused with INVALID_INPUT naming the path; the existing file is left alone. The contract records it being replaced
divergences.why: A read-only command, whose file name comes from whoever uploaded the attachment, must not change files already on disk.

divergences.old: confluence attachment download reporting saved with the platform's separator
divergences.toil: saved uses forward slashes on every platform; the file lands in the same place
divergences.why: Paths in JSON output are identical on Windows, macOS and Linux (CLAUDE.md, Cross-Platform). On macOS and Linux the separator is unchanged.

divergences.old: confluence attachment download reporting saved as --dir joined with the file name, so a relative --dir gives a relative path
divergences.toil: saved is always the absolute path written, with forward slashes, even when --dir is relative. The file lands in the same place (#233)
divergences.why: A relative --dir resolves against the workspace, which over MCP is not the caller's working directory, so a relative saved would point somewhere else. The absolute path says exactly where the file is.

divergences.old: The Confluence token falling back to the stored jira.apiToken, and a stored confluence.apiToken outranking the Jira env var
divergences.toil: Without a pairing, only the default connection borrows, and only TOIL_JIRA_API_TOKEN (the default Jira connection's env value), which outranks a stored Confluence token because env beats the file. A stored Jira token is used only when the connection names it with apiTokenFrom
divergences.why: A credential goes only to the connection it's configured on, or one the user paired it with (maintainer decision 7 on #68). The env-over-file order is core's single precedence rule for shared keys.

divergences.old: confluence page list, space list, page children, page labels, page comments and page attachments paging for as long as the server keeps sending _links.next, advancing start by the page's size
divergences.toil: start advances by the number of results read, and paging also stops on an empty page or after 1,000 pages (25,000 items) with an HTTP error naming the list and a fix to narrow it
divergences.why: A server that ignores start, or sends an empty page with a next link, would otherwise be asked for the same page forever. size equals the number of results on every real page.

divergences.old: confluence attachment download saving the attachment under the name the server gave it, once reduced to its last path segment
divergences.toil: A name Windows reserves for a device (CON, NUL, COM1 and the like, with any extension) is saved with a leading _, a : and everything after it is dropped, as are trailing dots and spaces, and the characters Windows forbids become _. filename in data is still the server's name; saved is where the file went. A --dir that names any of those is refused with INVALID_INPUT.
divergences.why: Windows reads each of those as a different file from the one named: a device, a stream inside an existing file, or the same name without its dots. The no-overwrite check has to see the file a write really lands on, and a name must work the same way on every platform.

divergences.old: confluence page create and page update with --markdown posting the Markdown to POST /rest/api/contentbody/convert/storage with representation "markdown", and sending the value Confluence returns as the body
divergences.toil: The Markdown is converted on this machine by the converter util md --to storage runs, which reads its output back as XML before returning it, and each code macro gets an ac:macro-id; no convert request is sent. What storage format can't hold, and any block that didn't survive the round trip, is a warning in meta.warnings (MD_LOSSY, MD_ROUNDTRIP_MISMATCH), and the page is still written (#519; #78 items 2 and 10)
divergences.why: Data Center documents no Markdown conversion on that endpoint (#78 item 2), and #519 reports it kept the escaped > of an autolink in the href, which failed XML validation. The maintainer chose toil's own converter ahead of a live check (2026-10-29, on #519), so the body sent is the one util md returns, and it is well-formed.
